extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NSF proposers (PIs), institutional Sponsored Projects Offices/Authorized Organizational Representatives (AORs), and institutional administrators preparing/submitting proposals to NSF
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting concept outlines, LOIs, preliminary proposals, and full proposals to the U.S. National Science Foundation, including eligibility, submission systems, required registrations/certifications, deadlines, and quality/conduct standards. Applies unless a program solicitation explicitly modifies these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Research.gov or Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specified in an NSF program solicitation, proposals submitted to NSF must be submitted via use of Research.gov or Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research.gov may be used for proposal preparation, submission, proposal file updates, and budgetary revisions; the policy and procedural guidance in Part I pertains to Research.gov submissions. Grants.gov submissions follow the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide and Grants.gov policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The full proposal should present the (1) objectives and scientific, engineering, or educational significance of the proposed work; (2) suitability of the methods to be employed; (3) qualifications of the investigator and the recipient organization; (4) effect of the activity on the infrastructure of science, engineering, and education, if applicable; and (5) amount of funding requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly present intellectual merit and broader impacts and be prepared with the care and thoroughness of a paper submitted for publication. Provide sufficient information to enable reviewers to evaluate the proposal according to NSF's merit review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Outline content and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A Concept Outline is a concise summary containing a title, proposed proposal type, information about prospective PI(s), potentially germane NSF organizational unit(s), keywords, a brief narrative description of the idea, and a brief description of how the idea fits the proposed proposal type or funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept Outlines are used to determine appropriateness for a funding opportunity; some programs require them and will only accept full proposals with a Program Officer Concurrence Email. They may be submitted by email or via ProSPCT; solicitations that require Concept Outlines will provide directions and length/format limits (generally two pages for email attachments or ~6000 characters in ProSPCT). Voluntary Concept Outlines may be used to obtain early feedback; a concurrence email is typically not provided for voluntary submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProSPCT webform and authentication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The ProSPCT webform uses structured fields, drop-down selections, validations, and text entry fields with character count limits to ensure minimal complete information prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProSPCT consists of a dashboard and webform; users must have a valid Login.gov account to access the tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Intent (LOI) content and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An LOI normally contains the PI’s names, a proposed title, a list of possible participating organizations (if applicable), and a one-page synopsis describing the work in sufficient detail to permit an appropriate selection of reviewers. An LOI is not a binding document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some solicitations require or request LOIs; failure to submit a required LOI identified in a solicitation will result in a full proposal not being accepted or returned without review. For collaborative proposals from multiple organizations, submit a single LOI for the entire project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary proposal preparation and decision types
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary proposals may be required to reduce proposers' effort, increase overall quality of full submissions, and assist NSF in managing reviews; content and submission requirements are specified in the program solicitation and prepared via Research.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two decision types: Invite/Not Invite (final decision affecting eligibility to submit a full proposal—only invited submitters may submit) and Encourage/Discourage (advisory only; both encouraged and discouraged submitters may submit full proposals). The solicitation specifies which decision mechanism applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program solicitation may override PAPPG provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A program solicitation may modify the general provisions of the PAPPG and, when it does, the solicitation's guidelines must be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of solicitation features that may deviate from PAPPG: restrict proposer categories; limit number of proposals per organization or PI; provide supplemental proposal preparation guidance; require letters of intent or preliminary proposals; include additional review criteria; require cost sharing; limit indirect (F&A) costs; specify additional award conditions or reporting requirements; anticipate use of cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of Institutions of Higher Education and related special instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Two- and four-year IHEs (including community colleges) accredited in, and having a campus located in the U.S., acting on behalf of their faculty members, are eligible to submit proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposal includes funding to an international branch campus of a U.S. IHE, the proposer must explain benefits to the project and justify why activities cannot be performed at the U.S. campus; include this information in the project description and check the appropriate box on the Cover Sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of non-profit, tribal, for-profit, state/local, foreign, and federal organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-profit/non-academic organizations and Tribal Nations are eligible. For-profit U.S.-based organizations, state and local governments, and foreign organizations may be eligible under specified conditions; other Federal agencies and FFRDCs are not normally supported but exceptions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For-profit organizations: may be funded in special cases or via specific funding opportunities. Foreign organizations: NSF rarely provides direct funding; cooperative projects with U.S. partners may be considered but support should generally be requested only for the U.S. portion. If funding a foreign organization or individual via subaward/consultant, the proposal must justify why in-country support is not feasible, why the foreign counterpart is more effective, what unique expertise/facilities/data/location they bring, and what significant opportunities they offer U.S. research/education; include this in the project description and check the 'Funding of a Foreign Organization or Foreign Individual' box on the Cover Sheet. Other Federal agencies may be eligible only under specified exceptions determined in advance by a cognizant NSF Program Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible proposers and restrictions on individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaffiliated individuals (including unaffiliated U.S. citizens) are not eligible to receive direct funding support from NSF. Individuals who are current parties to a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program are not eligible to serve as a senior/key person on an NSF proposal or award after May 20, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients of federal funds must demonstrate ability to comply with 2 CFR §200 requirements; an individual submitting a proposal to an NSF Postdoctoral Fellowship solicitation is not considered an unaffiliated individual. See Chapter II.D.1.e for details and required certifications associated with Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline, target date, and submission window definitions and local time rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Target dates are dates after which proposals will still be accepted (but may miss a meeting); Deadline Dates are dates after which proposals will not be accepted or will be returned without review; Submission Windows are periods during which proposals will be accepted and the end date converts to a Deadline Date for policy purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must be received by 5 p.m. submitting organization's local time on the established deadline date; if a deadline falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, it will be extended to the following business day. Letters of intent and preliminary proposals also follow the 5 p.m. local time standard. Target dates, deadlines, and windows are published in program descriptions, announcements, and solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special exceptions to deadline policy (natural or anthropogenic events and closures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility for meeting announced deadline dates may be granted with Program Officer approval in the occurrence of a natural or anthropogenic event that impacts ability to submit. NSF closure due to inclement weather or similar reasons automatically extends deadlines to the following business day after closure ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit after the deadline under this exception, proposers must check the 'Special Exception to the Deadline Date Policy' box on the NSF Cover Sheet and upload a statement identifying the nature of the event under Nature of Natural or Anthropogenic Event in the Single Copy Document section in Research.gov. If available, written Program Officer approval should be uploaded under Additional Single Copy Documents. Generally, NSF permits extension of the deadline by up to five business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on duplicate or substantially similar proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The same work/proposal cannot be funded twice; submission of duplicate or substantially similar proposals concurrently for review by more than one program will result in return of the redundant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposer envisions review by multiple programs, more than one program may be designated; but redundant submissions to multiple programs concurrently are prohibited (see Chapter IV.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) certifications and government-wide representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The AOR is required to provide certain NSF-specific proposal certifications during submission. Organizations must review and certify compliance with government-wide financial assistance representations and certifications maintained in SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification process occurs concurrently with submission. Failure to comply with SAM certification and registration requirements will impact submission and processing of proposals and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: UEI and SAM registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposers must provide a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) when submitting a new or renewal proposal or transfer of an award, and organizations registering to use NSF's electronic systems must have a valid and active SAM registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF validates UEI and SAM registration prior to allowing submission; if registration is not active, an organization cannot submit a proposal or receive award approval actions or payments. Subrecipients named in the proposal are required to obtain a UEI but do not need full SAM registration; GSA allows a process for subrecipients to receive a UEI without a complete SAM registration. SAM is the system of record for organizational information; maintain SAM registration with current information at all times while having an active award or a proposal under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF ID requirement and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: The NSF ID is a unique alpha-numeric identifier assigned to users by NSF and is used across NSF electronic systems as a login ID and identification verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each user should not have more than one NSF ID; users with multiple NSF IDs should contact the Help Desk for assistance. Submission of Social Security Numbers is requested only where necessary for business purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal receipt tracking and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, PIs can check the status of the proposal via NSF electronic systems; if a proposal number is not reflected, contact the Help Desk. Communications about the proposal should be addressed to the cognizant NSF Program Officer with reference to the proposal number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers are strongly encouraged to use NSF's electronic systems to verify the status of their submission to NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal processing timelines and award processing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers should allow up to six months for programmatic review and processing. The Division of Grants and Agreements generally makes awards within 30 calendar days after the program division/office makes its recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants/cooperative agreements for organizations that have not received an NSF award in five years or involving special situations may require additional review. Time-sensitive proposals (e.g., conference travel) will be accepted for review only if, in the Program Officer's opinion, they are received in sufficient time to permit appropriate review and processing to support the activity. Until an award is made, NSF is not responsible for costs incurred by the proposing organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of scholarship, attribution, and research misconduct policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF expects strict adherence to the rules of proper scholarship and attribution; all parts of the proposal should be prepared with equal care. Authors other than the PI (or co-PI) must be named and acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious failure to adhere to these standards can result in findings of research misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism) in proposing, performing, reviewing, or reporting research. Allegations are investigated by NSF's Office of Inspector General, and completed investigations are referred to NSF for action. Policies and procedures are discussed in Chapter XII.C and 45 CFR Part 689. Reporting results includes annual/final project reports and Project Outcomes Reports and publications arising from NSF-funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Metric System encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers are encouraged to use the Metric System (SI) of weights and measures in proposals submitted to the Foundation; recipients are encouraged to use metric units in reports, publications, and correspondence relating to proposals and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encouragement is pursuant to the Metric Conversion Act of 1975, as amended, and Executive Order 12770.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign organization/subaward justification content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposer includes funding for a foreign organization or foreign individual (via subaward or consultant arrangement), the proposal must justify the benefit to U.S. research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification must include at minimum: why in-country support is not feasible; why the foreign counterpart can carry out the activity more effectively than a U.S. organization/individual; what unique expertise, capability, facilities, data resources, and/or access to a geographic location the foreign party brings; and what significant science and engineering education, training, or research opportunities the foreign party offers to the U.S. This information must be included in the project description and the appropriate Cover Sheet box checked.
